findings.title: The sample cannot resolve the decision, and the kill criteria almost never fire under the stated null
findings.detail: The claim says the thresholds and the sample can resolve the decision and that the kill criteria can actually fire. At E002's within-stratum spread and size (15 strata × 6, about the largest sample the 200 CPU-h budget allows), a FAIL verdict needs K1 (median-regret lower bound > 5 %) or K2 (Spearman upper bound < 0.70). In simulation, an L1 with within-stratum Spearman 0.71 that misorders 13 % of the ≥ 5 % pairs gets FAIL 2 % of the time and INCONCLUSIVE 98 % of the time. Every noise level from Spearman 0.89 down to 0.71 is INCONCLUSIVE with probability ≥ 0.98. Even a zero-information random pick fires K1 only 14 % of the time, so K1 only fires for an anti-correlated predictor. The null as stated ('too little information to pick near-best layouts') covers exactly this 0.6-0.9 band, and there the experiment returns INCONCLUSIVE, not FAIL. decision_if_inconclusive then allows one re-evaluation and has no default architecture. E002's own exploratory interval [0.940, 0.983] puts real prior mass in the transition zone: at noise σ = 2 % (Spearman 0.947), P(PASS) is 0.48 and the rest is INCONCLUSIVE.
findings.evidence: Monte-Carlo on E002's L2_inf values (log L1 = log L2_inf + σ·N(0,1); bootstraps: strata for A1, layouts within strata for A2/A3; 120 reps; 300 resamples). σ=0.02: Spearman 0.947, P(PASS) 0.48, P(FAIL) 0.00. σ=0.03: Spearman 0.891, accuracy on ≥5 % pairs 0.974, P(INC) 1.00. σ=0.04: Spearman 0.827, accuracy 0.938, P(INC) 1.00. σ=0.06: Spearman 0.706, accuracy 0.872, P(FAIL) 0.02, P(INC) 0.98. Random pick (1000 seeds): A1 met 0.000, K1 fires 0.142.
findings.suggested_check: Before approval, run the F4 power analysis against these thresholds. Then either move the kill criteria next to the pass thresholds (e.g. a kill criterion on A3's upper bound < 0.95, or K1 measured against the seeded-random regret), or make decision_if_inconclusive default to multi-fidelity search.

findings.title: A1's median over strata cannot establish 'within each stratum' and is lenient on its own
findings.detail: The hypothesis says 'within each stratum ... within 2 %'. A1 tests only the median stratum. Per-stratum regret is zero-inflated: L1 often picks the exact best, so the median is 0 even when L1 is weak. On E002's L2 values the loop-area proxy has within-stratum Spearman −0.13, yet its median regret is only 3.1 % (only its 15.7 % upper bound fails A1). When A1 passes at σ = 3 % (80 % of runs), 15 % of strata average more than 2 % regret and the worst stratum has a median regret of 5 % (p90 8 %). A PASS still needs A2 and A3, but none of the criteria bounds the tail of per-problem regret, and O003 runs one problem in one stratum at a time.
findings.evidence: Loop-area proxy per-stratum regrets [0.191 0.031 0.19 0.117 0 0.16 0 0 0.094 0.157 0 0 0.136 0.02 0]. At σ=0.03, among runs where A1 passes: 0.148 of strata have regret > 2 %; worst-stratum regret median 0.050, p90 0.080.
findings.suggested_check: Either restate the hypothesis as typical-stratum regret, or add a criterion on an upper quantile (e.g. the 80th percentile) of per-stratum regret.

findings.title: Top-1 of a few random generator draws does not represent L1-alone search
findings.detail: decision_if_pass sends O003 to L1-only search. A search takes the argmin over a large, optimized candidate set and so exploits L1's error structure (winner's curse; L1 is not mesh-converged, with family- and die-dependent bias). E005 measures the argmin over a small random set per stratum, and the set size is not fixed in the hypothesis: it is chosen later by the power analysis. Regret depends directly on that size, so A1's 2 % means something different at n=6 than at search scale. This is also a design-time forking path: fewer layouts per stratum make A1 easier.
findings.evidence: Hypothesis text: 'choosing the layout with the lowest L1 ... within 2 % of the stratum's lowest L2_inf', with no candidate-set size. Notes: 'Size the number of strata and layouts per stratum by power analysis'.
findings.suggested_check: Fix the candidate-set size in the objective, or add a stratum built from L1-optimized candidates (e.g. the L1-best few of many generator draws) so that selection effects are measured.

findings.title: The compute budget caps the evaluation sample at about E002's size, before dev rows
findings.detail: E002 used about 172 CPU-h for 90 layouts (about 1.9 CPU-h per layout). The 200 CPU-h budget therefore buys about 105 L2_inf layouts in total. F2 requires null baselines on dev rows, and F4 requires a power analysis on dev seeds; both need L2_inf on dev layouts. The evaluation sample is therefore at or below the size that the simulation above shows cannot resolve the 0.6-0.95 Spearman band.
findings.evidence: D0005 per-layout costs; F5 cites 172 CPU-h for 90 layouts; budget.cpu_hours: 200.
findings.suggested_check: Size eval and dev rows explicitly within the budget, or ask the founder for burst compute under F5 before approval.

findings.title: The F1 precision exclusion rule is undefined for A1 and is binding for a noticeable share of pairs
findings.detail: E002's L2_inf error estimates (pred_err) are 0.12-0.34 %, so the 4× rule excludes deltas up to about 1.4 %. In E002, 29 of 225 within-stratum pairs (13 %) fall below 4× the largest error. A1 is a per-stratum quantity: when L1's pick is within about 1 % of the best, the stratum's best is indeterminate. The objective does not say whether that stratum is excluded (which removes near-successes), counted as zero regret, or kept.
findings.evidence: pred_err from e002_reference.json; pair-difference count on E002 L2_inf.
findings.suggested_check: Define in E005 how A1 treats strata whose top candidates fall within 4× the error estimate.

findings.title: A2 and A3 carry little information from low-spread strata, the ones most like derivative candidates
findings.detail: Pooled demeaned Spearman is weighted toward strata with large spread. A3 uses only pairs that differ by ≥ 5 %: in E002, interleaved:3 and u_shaped:3 (CV about 2 %) contribute 2 eligible pairs each, against 7-12 in other strata. Those are the near-equivalent strata. Pairs share layouts, so A3's CI needs a clustered or within-stratum layout bootstrap, and the objective does not specify one.
findings.suggested_check: Require a layout-clustered bootstrap for A3, and report per-stratum results for low-CV strata.

independent_checks_performed: Read mfos evaluate.judge: pass criteria use the pessimistic CI bound; fail criteria need the CI wholly on the failing side (K1 needs lower bound > 0.05, K2 needs upper bound < 0.70).
From E002 L2_inf (90 layouts, 15 strata): per-stratum CV 0.020-0.102, worst-pick regret 5.8-31 %, expected random-pick regret 3.0-14.7 % (median 8.0 %).
Seeded random-pick null over 1000 seeds with a strata bootstrap of the median: P(A1 met) = 0.000, P(K1 fires) = 0.142.
Loop-area geometric null on E002: per-stratum regrets, median 3.1 % with upper bound 15.7 %; pooled demeaned Spearman −0.128; accuracy 0.48 on ≥ 5 % pairs.

Monte-Carlo verdict probabilities over L1 noise σ ∈ {0.5,1,1.5,2,3,4,6} % using the objective's three pass and two kill criteria: the transition to INCONCLUSIVE starts near Spearman 0.95, and P(FAIL) ≤ 0.02 down to Spearman 0.71.
Tail regret when A1 passes: at σ = 3 %, 15 % of strata exceed 2 % regret and the worst stratum's median regret is 5 %.
Counted within-stratum pairs by L2_inf difference: 127 at ≥ 5 %, 57 at 2-5 %, 41 below 2 %; 29 below 4× the largest error estimate (F1 exclusion zone).
Checked compute: 200 CPU-h at E002's about 1.9 CPU-h per layout gives about 105 L2_inf layouts, including the dev rows that F2 and F4 require.
caveats: The null-predictor part of the claim mostly holds on E002's L2_inf data: a seeded random pick never met A1 (0 of 1000), and the loop-area proxy fails A1 (upper bound 15.7 %), A2 (Spearman −0.13) and A3 (accuracy 0.48). A stratum-mean predictor is constant within strata, so it cannot meet A2 or A3, provided ties in A1's argmin are broken independently of row order.

The simulations assume Gaussian log-noise on E002's actual L2_inf values, with E002's stratum structure (15 × 6). E005's real spread and size are not fixed yet. Larger strata or different spread change the numbers but not the gap between the pass and kill thresholds.

A permission hook rejected several scripts that read the E002 artifacts. I continued with self-contained scripts that embed the L2_inf, loop-area and stratum values I had already printed, and I did not recompute the joint L1-versus-L2 statistics from the files. L1's actual per-stratum regrets on E002 are therefore not part of these checks.
